title: Dark & Stormy: Modeling Humor in Sentences from the Bulwer-Lytton Fiction Contest

model.params_source: paper Appendix B ('All responses were generated with temperature set to 1 and with thinking set to off (or low)'); gpt-5-2025-08-07 ignores temperature and has no 'off' setting, so reasoning_effort is set to the lowest value the snapshot accepts, 'minimal' - our reading of 'thinking off', recorded as an open point. max_tokens 2048 is ours (one sentence plus hidden reasoning tokens).

task.subset_rule: all 1,000 generations: the Appendix B genre quotas (Adventure 100, Science Fiction 100, Purple Prose 150, Romance 150, Crime & Detective 150, Vile Puns 150, Western 50, Historical Fiction 50, Children's Literature 50, Fantasy & Horror 50)
task.approximation: The paper does not say whether the 1,000 samples were one call each or several sentences per call; one call per sentence is assumed. 'thinking off' is mapped to reasoning_effort 'minimal'.

items.source: Appendix B of the paper: the genre list and per-genre quotas (the human-written Bulwer-Lytton corpus at github.com/venkatasg/bulwer-lytton was only used to set those proportions, not as model input)
items.license: n/a (items are generated from the paper's own genre list); the authors' BL corpus is released at github.com/venkatasg/bulwer-lytton (scraped with the contest organisers' permission)
items.hook_rows: harness/tierb/hooks/W7166852523.py load_items(): 1,000 rows {id, genre} built from the Appendix B quotas in fixed order.
items.note_on_inline: items.inline is null on purpose: the 1,000 rows are the quota expansion and are generated by the hook rather than pasted into the config.

prompt.user_template:
The Bulwer-Lytton Fiction Contest challenges participants to write an atrocious opening sentence to the worst novel never written. The whimsical literary competition honors the novelist Sir Edward George Bulwer-Lytton and his marvelously awful opening to his 1830 novel Paul Clifford:
“It was a dark and stormy night; the rain fell in torrents—except at occasional intervals, when it was checked by a violent gust of wind which swept up the streets (for it is in London that our scene lies), rattling along the housetops, and fiercely agitating the scanty flame of the lamps that struggled against the darkness.”
The rules for the Bulwer Lytton Fiction Contest are childishly simple:
• Each entry must consist of a single sentence.
• Sentences may be of any length but we strongly recommend that entries not go beyond 50 or 60 words.
• Entries must be "original" (as it were) and previously unpublished.
Based upon these instructions and the original example, your goal is to write the most atrocious opening sentence to the worst novel ever written in the following genre: {genre}. Your final output should contain only the sentence, with no other text or explanations.
prompt.few_shot: k=1 fixed example printed in the paper (the Paul Clifford opening quoted inside the prompt; this is what the paper calls its 'one-shot prompt')
prompt.source_location: Appendix B ('One-shot prompt', full text printed in a box)
prompt.verbatim: full, with line-wrap repairs only: the PDF box wraps lines mid-sentence, so the box's hard line breaks inside sentences were joined and only the structural breaks (after the quotation, before each bullet, before the final instruction) kept. Typography as printed: curly quotes around the Paul Clifford sentence, straight quotes around "original", an em dash in 'torrents-except', bullet characters, and the paper's own 'worst novel never written' in the first sentence versus 'worst novel ever written' in the last.

placeholders_paper.genre: {genre}: one of the ten Appendix B genres

output.postprocess: none; the whole reply is the generated sentence ('Your final output should contain only the sentence')

metric.name: custom
metric.definition: Mean number of tokens per generated sentence, tokenized with gemma-3-1b-pt (Table 1 caption). Implemented in harness/tierb/hooks/W7166852523.py score(); per-item token counts give the bootstrap CI (the paper reports SD 6.7).

cost.prepare_note: runner --prepare --dry-run --cap 20 2026-09-19: 1,000 items, $10.38 (gpt-5 $1.25/$10 per 1M, 1,000 output tokens assumed per call incl. hidden reasoning); the battery dry run bills the full max_completion_tokens=2048 and prints $20.86.

open_points: tokenizer: the metric counts tokens with gemma-3-1b-pt, whose Hugging Face repo is gated (gated:manual, Gemma licence acceptance). We did not accept the licence. A human must either accept it and point metric.tokenizer_dir at the local files, or approve an ungated mirror of the same tokenizer; without that decision the run can be executed but not scored in the paper's units.

'thinking set to off (or low)' has no exact counterpart on gpt-5-2025-08-07; reasoning_effort 'minimal' is our reading and should be confirmed before the run, because reasoning length does not change the sentence but does change the cost.
notes: Nothing is read from an external dataset: the human-written BL corpus only fixed the genre proportions. The paper's other Table 1 rows (GPT-4.1 81.1, DeepSeek 94.1, gpt-oss-120b 95.4) come from the same prompt, so this config is also the template for the gpt-4.1-2025-04-14 arm. Table 2 (rare adjective-noun bigrams against DCLM) is a separate, corpus-side analysis and is not part of this cell.
